record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure labels and OCR-rendered notation are garbled, but the main text and reported comparisons are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments comparing Hessian-based sharpness with generalization and argues that sharper solutions can generalize better, refining or challenging the use of these measures as generalization indicators. It does not test the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper measures Hessian sharpness and validation performance under weight decay and optimizer changes. These results bear on generalization measures, but the paper does not test the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7 or the other listed version-specific claims.
record.test_reason: The optimizer comparisons test V4's qualified claim: a tuned adaptive recipe combining Adam, decoupled weight decay and iterate averaging outperforms SGD on held-out accuracy. The Hessian experiments do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that conventional Hessian sharpness can decrease as cross-entropy loss decreases and weights grow, demonstrate better-generalizing yet sharper solutions under weight decay and adapted optimization, and question these measures' usefulness for generalization. This does not establish failure of V7's magnitude-aware measure.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments compare Hessian-based sharpness and validation performance across regularization and optimizer conditions; they do not reproduce the magnitude-aware perturbation method in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The relationship changes with L2 regularization, optimizer choice, dataset, and batch normalization evaluation versus train mode. Batch norm evaluation mode magnifies the reported sharpness differences.

fits_no_version.finding: Better validation performance accompanies larger conventional Hessian sharpness measures under weight decay and optimizer changes; changing batch-normalization evaluation mode can magnify curvature differences.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian spectral and Frobenius measures do not consistently rank generalization performance across the tested training recipes.

record.problems: The study uses Lanczos spectral approximations and notes that taking more or fewer Lanczos steps can alter results; eigenvalue mass near the origin may split. Some results are reported in figures, and the batch norm evaluation comparison contains an internally inconsistent repeated reference to the regularized solution. Experiments are limited to the reported architectures, datasets, and training schedules.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The study discusses random-label memorization, adaptive optimizers, and other generalization results from cited work in its introduction and related work; these are not its own results and were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes.
Test-error trends as width increases beyond interpolation.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning; isolated effects of broader tuning, decoupled decay or switching; language benchmarks.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, strength and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Its Gadam comparisons are experiments using a previously introduced optimizer, not merely cited performance. No tools or external sources were used.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance under the specified tuning conditions.
Large-batch training and its generalization gap.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
